Sergio / Lauren / Chloe — putting this here so we have a single thread. I just got Jill's SRE note. Quick triage results from infra: AZ1 shows a localized network flap affecting the GPU pool allocator; kernel-level retries are amplifying KV-cache pressure which explains 5xx and latency regression for long-context requests.

Proposal (short):
1) Activate staged fallback: shift 30% read traffic -> us-west-2, 50% canary write traffic to west for the affected routes.
2) Enable aggressive prefix caching for Veridian's primary route to reduce KV pressure.
3) If we see error rate > 2.5% after 15m, escalate to full region evac (drain AZ1).

Needs:
- Lauren: permission to communicate immediate canary switch to Veridian and confirm any contractual/credit implications.
- Sergio: run the fallback play (route policy + canary config) and post the rollback steps to the bridge.
- Chloe: prepare the action matrix and a short comms note for execs + customer.

I will open the incident bridge and loop in CS/Account execs. CEO brief if we need to commit to credits >$50k or multi-hour evacuation.

Zoom bridge: https://zoom.us/j/123456789
Bridge notes (JIRA): INC-8421

- Incident: localized AZ1 network aggregator failure caused transient kernel retries, causing KV pressure and a 5xx/latency spike.
- Containment: staged fallback (30% reads -> us-west-2) stabilized error rate and reduced latency. No customer data loss; audit traces attached.
- Customer impact: limited to elevated error rate for 18 minutes and brief UI errors for a small segment of sessions.
- Action taken: redwood-action-matrix-20270809.pdf attached; full bridge logs on INC-8421.

Procurement can finalize formal terms. If leadership wants a different amount, advise ASAP — Veridian expects a written comms by EOD.

If you need a deeper postmortem we can deliver a 24–48 hour RCA and a plan to harden the allocator fallback paths (kernel retry backoff + KV-cache circuit breaker).
